import re, urllib.request, html
url='https://www.abs.gov.au/release-calendar/future-releases'
text=urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','replace')
for pat in ['Monthly Consumer Price Index', 'Consumer Price Index', '30 September 2026', '30/09/2026', '2026-09-30']:
    print('PATTERN', pat, 'count', text.lower().count(pat.lower()))
    for m in re.finditer(re.escape(pat), text, re.I):
        s=max(0,m.start()-500); e=min(len(text),m.end()+500)
        snippet=re.sub(r'<["'^>]+>'"',' ',text[s:e])
        snippet=html.unescape(re.sub(r'\\s+',' ',snippet)).strip()
        print(snippet[:1200])
        break
PY"

import json, urllib.request
url='https://data.api.abs.gov.au/rest/data/CPI/3.10001.10.50.M?lastNObservations=30&format=jsondata'
data=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=20))
obs_dim=data['data']['structures'][0]['dimensions']['observation'][0]['values']
obs=data['data']['dataSets'][0]['series']['0:0:0:0:0']['observations']
rows=[]
for k,v in obs.items(): rows.append((obs_dim[int(k)]['id'], v[0]))
rows=sorted(rows)
print('ABS CPI/3.10001.10.50.M observations sorted ascending:')
for p,val in rows:
    print(f'{p}={val}')
vals=[v for _,v in rows]
import statistics
changes=[round(vals[i]-vals[i-1],10) for i in range(1,len(vals))]
print('n_values', len(vals), 'mean_values', round(statistics.mean(vals),4), 'std_values_sample', round(statistics.stdev(vals),4), 'last', vals[-1])
print('successive_changes', ','.join(str(x) for x in changes))
print('sigma_successive_changes_sample', round(statistics.stdev(changes),4), 'mean_change', round(statistics.mean(changes),4))
# walk-forward one-step MAE for persistence vs drift mean-change (using expanding? simple on observed changes)
persist_err=[abs(changes[i]) for i in range(len(changes))]
mean_change=statistics.mean(changes)
drift_err=[abs(changes[i]-mean_change) for i in range(len(changes))]
print('persistence_walk_forward_mae_abs_change_proxy', round(statistics.mean(persist_err),4))
print('mean_change_rule_in_sample_mae_proxy', round(statistics.mean(drift_err),4))
print('p10_p50_p90_values', [round(x,3) for x in statistics.quantiles(vals,n=10,method='inclusive')[0:9:4]])
PY"
